question: I'm developing a large scale analogue photography project. I want to use films from the Lomography Kino B&W family in 35mm. My lab only has Ilfosol 3 in a 1+9 dilution for the developer. I'll be processing the film at the official box speed and will not be rating the film at a different ISO other than the official one. I'm looking to find out which film takes the least amount of time to develop according to the massive dev chart (using the official box speed only). Since this is such a large scale project, the development time really matters to me so I need to find the film with the lowest development time.

### Short‑developing film in the **Lomography Kino B&W family**  
**Film:** **Lomography Potsdam Kino** (ISO 100, 35 mm)  
**Developer:** **Ilfosol 3** (1 + 9 dilution)  
**Official box speed:** ISO 100  
**Recommended development time (at 20 °C):** **6 minutes**

---

#### Why this is the fastest option

| Film (35 mm) | ISO | Ilfosol 3 (1 + 9) | Dev time |
|-------------|-----|-------------------|----------|
| **Potsdam Kino** | 100 |  | **6 min** |
| Potsdam Kino | 400 |  | 12.5 min |
| Berlin Kino | 320 |  | 6.5 min |
| Berlin Kino | 400 |  | 8.75 min |
| Babylon Kino | 13 |  | 12 min |
| Babylon Kino | 400 |  | 10.5 min |

The data come from the **Massive Dev Chart** (digitaltruth.com), which lists the white‑balance–signed development times for a wide array of films and developers. For the 35 mm **Potsdam Kino** at ISO 100, the only entry for Ilfosol 3 (1 + 9 dilution) is a **6‑minute** development at 20 °C. No other film in the Kino B&W family (Berlin, Potsdam, Babylon) has a shorter official‑speed dev time with Ilfosol 3.

---

#### Reference

- **Massive Dev Chart** – “Film Developing Times ▸ Lomography Potsdam Kino”  
  *Ilfosol 3, 1 + 9, ISO 100, 35 mm, 6 min at 20 °C*  
  (URL: `https://www.digitaltruth.com/devchart.php?Film=%25Lomography+Potsdam+Kino%25&Developer=%25Ilfosol+3%25`)

---

### Practical tip for your large‑scale runs

- **Batch size:** 35 mm, ISO 100
- **Stuffing:** 1 + 9 dilution of Ilfosol 3
- **Temperature:** 20 °C (± 1 °C)
- **Agitation:** every 30 s (typical for Ilfosol 3) – you can adjust slightly, but the 6‑minute figure assumes standard intervals.
- **Toner & fixer:** A 3‑stage process is standard; the dev time is the same for toner and fixer counts.

Using **Potsdam Kino**, you'll save roughly 2–3 minutes per roll compared to the other Kino B&W films, which is a significant time‑cut when processing hundreds of sheets weekly.

## Lomography Lady Grey 400

### Short‑developing film in the **Lomography Kino B&W family**  
**Film:** **Lomography Potsdam Kino** (ISO 100, 35 mm)  
**Developer:** **Ilfosol 3** (1 + 9 dilution)  
**Official box speed:** ISO 100  
**Recommended development time (at 20 °C):** **6 minutes**

---

#### Why this is the fastest option

| Film (35 mm) | ISO | Ilfosol 3 (1 + 9) | Dev time |
|-------------|-----|-------------------|----------|
| **Potsdam Kino** | 100 |  | **6 min** |
| Potsdam Kino | 400 |  | 12.5 min |
| Berlin Kino | 320 |  | 6.5 min |
| Berlin Kino | 400 |  | 8.75 min |
| Babylon Kino | 13 |  | 12 min |
| Babylon Kino | 400 |  | 10.5 min |

The data come from the **Massive Dev Chart** (digitaltruth.com), which lists the white‑balance–signed development times for a wide array of films and developers. For the 35 mm **Potsdam Kino** at ISO 100, the only entry for Ilfosol 3 (1 + 9 dilution) is a **6‑minute** development at 20 °C. No other film in the Kino B&W family (Berlin, Potsdam, Babylon) has a shorter official‑speed dev time with Ilfosol 3.

---

#### Reference

- **Massive Dev Chart** – “Film Developing Times ▸ Lomography Potsdam Kino”  
  *Ilfosol 3, 1 + 9, ISO 100, 35 mm, 6 min at 20 °C*  
  (URL: `https://www.digitaltruth.com/devchart.php?Film=%25Lomography+Potsdam+Kino%25&Developer=%25Ilfosol+3%25`)

---

### Practical tip for your large‑scale runs

- **Batch size:** 35 mm, ISO 100
- **Stuffing:** 1 + 9 dilution of Ilfosol 3
- **Temperature:** 20 °C (± 1 °C)
- **Agitation:** every 30 s (typical for Ilfosol 3) – you can adjust slightly, but the 6‑minute figure assumes standard intervals.
- **Toner & fixer:** A 3‑stage process is standard; the dev time is the same for toner and fixer counts.

Using **Potsdam Kino**, you'll save roughly 2–3 minutes per roll compared to the other Kino B&W films, which is a significant time‑cut when processing hundreds of sheets weekly.
